text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/01/17 - Essay - 01
Furniture, light and space shape an everyday room.
Pexels · 13977663
Making a room your own
There is more than one way to arrange a room. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful starting
points.
One reason is that giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use. For instance, we keep keys in a bowl beside
the door. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that small personal choices make a space feel familiar. For example, we place a favourite photograph where we
can see it from our chair. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people
may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Compare two ways to arrange a room: a rigid plan and one that allows adjustment. Assess one advantage and one limitation. Use four
short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss
giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use with an example; discuss small personal choices make a space
feel familiar with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
